theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What does "rooming" a guest mean?
options: Cleaning the room before the guest arrives
Moving a guest to a cheaper room when it is full
Taking a guest to their room and showing its features
Checking the room for damage after check-out

questions.stem: Before guests come, where do you find who is arriving today and any special requests?
options: The lost and found book
The arrivals list
The maintenance log
The staff rota

questions.stem: On the room status report, what does "VC" mean?
options: Very clean, kept for a VIP
Vacant and clean, ready to sell
Visitor checked in and staying
Vacant, but still needs cleaning

questions.stem: Why do you check that the room is shown as clean and inspected before you room a guest?
options: So that the guest is not taken to a room that is not ready
So that housekeeping can start cleaning once the guest is in
So that you know how much to charge for room service
So that you can tell the guest which staff cleaned it

questions.stem: The arrivals list shows a family has asked for a baby cot. When should it be put in the room?
options: After the family asks for it again at the desk
Before they arrive, when the room is prepared
Only after the family has unpacked their bags
Next morning, when housekeeping does its rounds

questions.stem: A VIP is arriving. What extra may be placed in the room before arrival, as the property's standard says?
options: The bill for the stay, so it can be paid
Another guest's luggage, to save a trip
A welcome amenity, such as fruit and a card
A spare set of all the keys for that floor

questions.stem: Two families have booked "connecting rooms". What are connecting rooms?
options: Rooms on different floors that have the same view
Two rooms side by side with a door between them
Two rooms that share one bathroom across a hall
Rooms that face each other across the corridor

questions.stem: The desk agent gives you the key card folder for a guest. How is the room number given to the guest?
options: Written on the folder and shown quietly, never said aloud
Called out loud so that the guest hears it across the lobby
Written on the key card itself with a marker pen
Said aloud to the bell staff in front of other guests

questions.stem: How should you introduce yourself to the guest before you set off for the room?
options: Smile, greet the guest by name and give your own name
Take the bags and walk off, so that the guest follows
Ask the guest for a tip before you set off together
Tell the guest how busy and tired you have been today

questions.stem: Which name should you use for the guest while you room them?
options: Their first name only, to be friendly
Their title and surname, such as Mr Brown
A pet name, such as "boss" or "darling"
Their room number, so it stays private

questions.stem: At a hotel with bell staff, who normally carries the luggage when a guest is roomed?
options: The guest, while the staff lead the way
The housekeeper who works that floor
The front desk agent, leaving the desk
The bell attendant, using a trolley

questions.stem: Before you leave the lobby, what should you check about the guest's luggage?
options: That every bag is open so that you can look inside
That each bag weighs less than 10 kg before lifting
That the guest has paid a fee for each bag carried
The number of pieces and any damage, with the guest

questions.stem: How should you lift a heavy suitcase onto the trolley?
options: Bend at the waist with straight legs and pull it up fast
Bend your knees, keep your back straight, hold it close
Twist your body round as you lift, to save a step
Lift it above your head and swing it onto the trolley

questions.stem: How should luggage be loaded on a luggage trolley?
options: Small, light bags at the bottom and heavy ones on top
Piled as high as it will go, so only one trip is made
Heavy cases at the bottom, fragile ones on top
Garment bags folded flat under the heavy suitcases

questions.stem: A guest wants to carry her own handbag and laptop bag. What should you do?
options: Insist on carrying them; it is your job
Take them anyway when she is not looking
Respect her wish and carry the other bags
Refuse to carry any of her luggage

questions.stem: Where should you walk as you take the guest to the room?
options: Slightly ahead and to one side, leading the way
Far behind, so that the guest finds the room alone
Running ahead to open the door before they come
Beside the guest's partner, chatting about yourself

questions.stem: On the way to the room, what should you point out to the guest?
options: The staff-only areas and the cleaning store
Other guests' rooms and who is staying in them
The restaurant, pool and other facilities
The manager's office and the staff canteen

questions.stem: You reach the lift (elevator) with the guest. What should you do?
options: Get in first yourself and stand near the door
Hold the door and let the guest enter first
Push the trolley in first, then call the guest
Take the stairs and meet the guest upstairs

questions.stem: The guest has a lot of luggage and the lift is small. What is best?
options: Squeeze the guest in beside the full luggage trolley
Leave all the luggage in the lobby until the next day
Ask the guest to carry the heaviest bags upstairs
Send the bags in another lift and meet at the room

questions.stem: The guest asks what time the restaurant closes, and you are not sure. What should you do?
options: Guess a time, so the guest is not kept waiting
Say that it is not your job to know about that
Say you will find out and let them know soon
Tell them to ask one of the other guests instead

questions.stem: The guest looks very tired after a long flight. How should you room them?
options: Give a full tour of the grounds first
Keep it short, and offer to explain more later
Leave them to rest in the lobby first
Talk about every activity on offer that week

questions.stem: You reach the room. What should you do before the guest walks in?
options: Walk in first and close the door behind you at once
Hand the key to the guest and leave at once
Knock, open the door, turn on lights, step aside
Leave the luggage outside the door in the corridor

questions.stem: Why do you knock before you open the room, even though it should be empty?
options: To let the floor housekeeper know a guest is coming
Because the key card will not work unless you knock
To test whether the door is strong and closes well
In case the room was let in error and is in use

questions.stem: Where should the guest's suitcases be placed in the room?
options: On the bed, so that the guest can unpack quickly
In the bathroom, out of the way of the door
On the luggage rack, not on the bed
In the corridor, for the guest to bring in later

questions.stem: Which room features should you explain to the guest?
options: The private phone numbers of the housekeeping staff
How to take the furniture apart for cleaning it
The air conditioning, lights, phone, safe and Wi-Fi
The prices that other guests paid for their rooms

questions.stem: How should you explain the in-room safe to the guest?
options: Set your own code in it, so that you can help later
Tell the guest to leave the safe open all the time
Ask the guest to tell you the code they will use
Show how to set a private code, without watching

questions.stem: What does the plan on the inside of the room door usually show?
options: The fire escape route from that room
The names of the staff on that floor
The restaurant's menu for the day
The room rates for every room type

questions.stem: A guest asks how to call the front desk from the room phone. What should you do?
options: Tell them to use their own mobile phone instead
Say that they should come down to the lobby each time
Tell them every call costs money, so not to use it
Show the number on the phone card and how to dial

questions.stem: The property charges for minibar items. What should you tell the guest about the minibar?
options: Where the price list is, and that items are charged
Everything in it is free and is refilled every hour
It is for staff use only and must not be opened
That they must pay cash each time they open it

questions.stem: What is the "Do Not Disturb" sign used for?
options: To ask housekeeping to clean the room first
To ask staff not to knock or enter for now
To show that the guest has checked out early
To warn other guests that the floor is wet

questions.stem: Why should you show the guest how to lock the balcony or patio door?
options: So the guest can lock staff out
So that the air conditioning stops working
To keep the room and the guest's things secure
So that housekeeping cannot clean the balcony

questions.stem: How do you explain the air conditioning to a guest?
options: Set it to the coldest and tell them not to change it
Say that it must stay off while the guest is out
Tell them it is broken so that they do not touch it
Show the controls and how to change the temperature

questions.stem: By the door there is a key-card slot that controls the room's power. What should you show the guest?
options: Put the key card in the slot to switch on the power
Leave the slot empty, or the key card will be wiped
Use a coin in the slot to turn on the lights
Never touch the slot, as it is for staff only

questions.stem: You open the door and find the room has not been cleaned. What should you do?
options: Leave the guest there and send housekeeping up later
Apologise, step out with the guest and call the desk
Tell the guest it is fine and tidy it up yourself
Ask the guest to wait in the room while it is cleaned

questions.stem: The guest booked a king bed but the room has two single beds. What should you do?
options: Apologise and call the desk to arrange the right room
Push the two beds together and say it is just the same
Tell the guest that this was all that was available
Tell them to change rooms themselves the next day

questions.stem: While rooming the guest, you notice the bathroom tap is leaking. What should you do?
options: Tell the guest it will be reported, then report it
Ignore it, as the guest may not even notice the leak
Try to repair it yourself while the guest watches you
Tell the guest to report it if it gets any worse

questions.stem: A guest is unhappy with the view and asks for another room. What should you do?
options: Tell them that every room has the same view
Promise them the best suite at no extra charge
Move their luggage to an empty room you choose
Call the front desk to see what is available

questions.stem: You have explained the room. What should you do before you leave?
options: Wait by the door until the guest gives you a tip
Sit down and chat until the guest asks you to go
Leave without a word, so as not to disturb them at all
Ask if they need anything else, and wish them well

questions.stem: A guest offers you a tip at the end of rooming. What is the right response?
options: Thank them, and follow the property's tipping policy
Ask for more, because the bags were heavy to carry
Refuse it rudely, so that they know you are proud
Count it in front of the guest before saying thank you

questions.stem: How should you leave the room?
options: Leave the door wide open for the guest
Slam the door so that it is sure to lock
Leave the luggage trolley in the room
Close the door gently and quietly behind you

questions.stem: After rooming a guest, what do you write on the rooming slip or bell log?
options: The guest's credit card number and its expiry date
The guest's passport number and home address
What the guest wore and what they talked about
The room, the time, how many bags, and your name

questions.stem: Why is a record of each rooming kept?
options: To work out how much tip each bell attendant earned
So the desk can trace who roomed whom, and when
So that guests can see who carried other guests' bags
So that staff are paid by the number of bags carried

questions.stem: During rooming the guests tell you it is their wedding anniversary. What should you do?
options: Keep it to yourself, because it is private
Post it on social media to promote the hotel
Ask how many years they have been married, then forget it
Congratulate them and tell the desk, so it can be noted

questions.stem: At a private villa, rooming the guests usually also includes:
options: Showing them where the staff sleep and eat
Collecting all their passports for the stay
Introducing the staff and explaining the house
Asking them to sign for the keys to the staff rooms

questions.stem: At a villa, what should you explain to the guests on arrival, as the villa's own rules say?
options: The gate, the alarm, the pool rules and calling staff
The private bank details of the villa owner
How much each member of the villa staff is paid
Which bedrooms the owner's family use

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters VIP stand for?
On the arrivals list, what do the letters ETA stand for?
What is the list called that shows which room each member of a tour group will have?
Which two-letter room status code means the room is empty but still needs cleaning?
What is a room called that cannot be sold because it needs repair?
What is a guest called who arrives without a booking?
What is the folding extra bed on wheels that can be brought to a room called?
What is the label tied to each bag, showing the guest's name and room, called?
What is the lift called that is used by staff and for luggage, not by guests?
What is the small lens in the room door, through which the guest can see who is outside, called?
What is the folder or booklet in the room, with the property's services, phone numbers and menus, called?
Besides the network name, what must you give the guest so they can join the property's Wi-Fi?
What is it called when a guest asks the desk to phone the room to wake them at a set time?
What is the time called by which guests must leave their room on the last day of their stay?
A European guest asks about the plugs. What is the frequency of Jamaica's mains supply, in hertz?

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare before rooming a guest who is due to arrive this afternoon.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the arrivals list for the guest's name, expected time of arrival, number of guests, room type and any special requests, such as a baby cot, a rollaway bed, a high floor or a ground-floor room. I check the room status with housekeeping to make sure the room is clean, inspected and ready. If there are requests or a VIP amenity, such as fruit and a welcome card, I check that they are in the room before the guest arrives. I make sure the luggage trolley is clean and free, and that I know about the room's features, such as the safe, Wi-Fi and air conditioning. I check that I am well groomed, in clean uniform with my name badge. When the guest checks in, I collect the key card folder from the desk and confirm the room number quietly, without saying it aloud.
markingPoints: Checks the arrivals list: name, time, room type and requests
Confirms the room is clean, inspected and ready
Checks special requests and amenities are in place before arrival
Gets equipment ready (clean trolley) and knows the room's features
Good grooming; collects the key folder and keeps the room number private

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would room a guest from the front desk to the room.
essays.modelAnswer: When the guest has checked in, I greet them by title and surname, smile and introduce myself. I take the key card folder from the desk agent and never say the room number aloud. I count the luggage with the guest, check for damage and load it safely on the trolley. I walk slightly ahead to lead the way, at the guest's pace, and point out the restaurant, pool, lifts and other facilities on the way. At the lift I hold the door and let the guest in first and out first. At the room I knock, open the door, switch on the lights and step aside to let the guest in. I put the bags on the luggage rack. I explain the room features: air conditioning, lights, key-card power slot, phone, safe, Wi-Fi, TV, minibar and the fire escape plan. I ask if they need anything else, hand over the key, wish them a pleasant stay, close the door quietly and record the rooming in the bell log.
markingPoints: Greets by name, introduces self, keeps the room number private
Counts and checks the luggage and loads it safely
Leads the way, points out facilities, correct lift manners
Knocks, opens, lights on, lets the guest in; bags on the rack
Explains features, offers further help, leaves politely and records the rooming

essays.stem: Explain which features of the room you would show the guest during rooming, and why each one matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I show the key-card power slot and the light switches, so the guest can use the room straight away. I show how to work the air conditioning and change the temperature, because guests arriving in the Jamaican heat want to be comfortable. I show the phone and the numbers for the front desk and room service, so the guest can get help at any time. I explain how to set a private code on the in-room safe, without watching, so that passports and money are secure. I give the Wi-Fi name and password. I point out the TV, the minibar and where its price list is, and the guest directory. I show how to lock the balcony door and the main door, with the peephole and security chain, for the guest's safety. I point out the fire escape plan on the door. Last, I show the bathroom, towels and hot water. All this saves the guest calls and worry and keeps them safe.
markingPoints: Power slot, lights and air conditioning for comfort
Phone and key numbers so the guest can get help
Safe (private code) and door and balcony locks for security
Wi-Fi, TV, minibar charges and the guest directory
Fire escape plan; says why: comfort, safety and fewer problems

essays.stem: Explain how you keep the guest, their room and their belongings safe and private during rooming.
essays.modelAnswer: I never say the room number aloud in the lobby or lift, where others could hear it. The desk agent writes it on the key folder, not on the key card itself, so a lost card does not show which room it opens. I keep the guest's luggage with me at all times and never leave it unattended in the lobby or corridor. I count the bags with the guest at the start and in the room, so nothing goes missing. In the room I show how to use the safe with their own private code and do not watch them set it. I show the door lock, the peephole and the security chain, and how to lock the balcony door. I point out the fire escape plan. I do not talk about the guest or their room to other guests or outsiders. After rooming I record only what the property needs, such as the room, time and number of bags.
markingPoints: Room number never said aloud; written on the folder, not the card
Luggage never left unattended; counted at the start and in the room
Safe shown without watching the code
Door lock, peephole, chain, balcony lock and fire plan explained
Guest details kept confidential; only the needed record kept

essays.stem: You open the door and the room is not right: it has not been cleaned, or it has the wrong beds. Describe what you would do.
essays.modelAnswer: I stay calm and polite and do not blame anyone. I apologise to the guest sincerely and do not leave them in a room that is not ready. If the room has not been cleaned, I step out with the guest and their luggage and close the door. I call the front desk at once from a house phone or radio and explain the problem quietly. The desk will find another ready room of the right type or arrange for housekeeping to finish quickly. While we wait I offer the guest a seat in the lobby or bar and, if the property allows, a welcome drink. I keep the guest's luggage with me and safe. When the new room is ready, I collect the new key folder, room the guest there and explain its features. Afterwards I report what happened to my supervisor so that the cause can be found and put right.
markingPoints: Stays calm, apologises and does not blame anyone
Does not leave the guest in an unready room; keeps the luggage safe
Calls the front desk to find the right room
Makes the guest comfortable while waiting
Rooms the guest in the new room and reports the problem

essays.stem: Explain how you handle a guest's luggage safely during rooming, for yourself and for the guest's belongings.
essays.modelAnswer: Before lifting, I check how heavy and what shape each bag is. I bend my knees, keep my back straight, hold the bag close to my body and lift with my legs, without twisting. For very heavy bags I get help or use the trolley. I load the trolley with heavy cases at the bottom, light and fragile bags on top and garment bags hanging, without piling it so high that I cannot see. I count the pieces with the guest and point out any damage before I move them, so the guest knows I did not cause it. I push the trolley, not pull it, at a steady pace and take care on ramps and at doors. I never leave the luggage alone. In the room, I place the bags on the luggage rack or on the floor, never on the bed, and I count them again with the guest.
markingPoints: Safe lifting: knees bent, back straight, load close, no twisting; help for heavy bags
Loads the trolley correctly: heavy at the bottom, fragile on top, can see over it
Counts pieces and notes damage with the guest
Never leaves luggage unattended; moves the trolley with care
Places bags on the rack, not the bed, and counts again

essays.stem: A wedding party of 20 guests arrives together. Describe how rooming a group is different and how you would organise it.
essays.modelAnswer: With a group, I cannot walk every guest to the room one at a time, so planning is important. Before they arrive, I get the rooming list from the front desk, showing each guest's name and room. I make sure the rooms are ready and that any amenities, such as a welcome card for the couple, are in place. When the group arrives, the desk or group leader hands out the key folders, often in a quiet area so room numbers stay private. I tag each bag with the guest's name and room number from the rooming list and count all the pieces. The guests may go up on their own or in small groups with staff, while the bell team delivers the tagged luggage to each room soon after. I record the delivery of each bag in the bell log and report any missing or extra pieces to the supervisor.
markingPoints: Gets the rooming list in advance and checks the rooms are ready
Key folders given out quietly, keeping room numbers private
Tags and counts every bag against the rooming list
Guests go up in small groups while luggage is delivered promptly
Records deliveries and reports missing or extra bags

essays.stem: Explain how rooming guests at a private villa is different from rooming a guest at a large hotel.
essays.modelAnswer: At a hotel, a bell attendant takes one guest or family to one room and explains that room. At a villa, the guests usually rent the whole house, so rooming means a welcome and a tour of the whole property. I greet the party at the gate or door with a welcome drink and introduce the villa staff, such as the butler, cook and housekeeper. I help carry the luggage to the bedrooms the guests choose, often with the lead guest deciding who sleeps where. I explain the house: the gate and alarm, door and window locks, air conditioning, the pool and its safety rules, the generator or water heater if there is one, mosquito nets and how to call staff at night. I agree meal times and menus with the guests. The welcome is more personal, and the staff will serve the same party throughout their stay.
markingPoints: Hotel: one room explained; villa: tour of the whole house
Welcomes the party and introduces the villa staff
Helps guests choose bedrooms and carries luggage
Explains security, pool rules, utilities and how to call staff
More personal service; agrees meal times and needs with the guests

essays.stem: Explain what you record and report after rooming a guest, and why these records are kept.
essays.modelAnswer: After rooming, I fill in the bell log or rooming slip with the room number, the time, the number of bags and my name. If the guest is a VIP or part of a group, I note that too. I report anything I noticed in the room that needs fixing, such as a leaking tap, a light that does not work or a missing towel, so that maintenance or housekeeping can put it right quickly. I pass on any request the guest made, such as an extra pillow or a wake-up call, and any special occasion, such as a birthday or anniversary, so the property can mark it. If the guest was unhappy, I tell my supervisor. These records help trace luggage if it goes missing, show who was in the room and when, help the team give good service and protect staff if there is a complaint later.
markingPoints: Records room, time, number of bags and staff name
Reports faults to maintenance or housekeeping
Passes on requests and special occasions
Reports any unhappy guest to the supervisor
Explains why: tracing luggage, security, service and protecting staff

essays.stem: Describe how you would room a guest who uses a wheelchair, making sure they are safe and comfortable.
essays.modelAnswer: Before arrival, I check that the room is an accessible room, if one was booked, with wide doors, a roll-in shower, grab rails and a lower bed and switches. When the guest arrives, I greet them at eye level where I can, and speak to the guest, not only to their companion. I ask how they would like to be helped and do not push the wheelchair unless they ask me to. I take the luggage on the trolley and use the lift and ramps, not the stairs, and check the route is clear of obstacles. In the room, I make sure there is space to move, and I put the bags where the guest can reach them. I show the accessible features, such as the grab rails, the emergency call cord if there is one, and the safe at a low level. I explain the emergency procedure for guests who cannot use the stairs, and I tell the front desk so that it is noted for an emergency.
markingPoints: Checks an accessible room is ready before arrival
Speaks to the guest directly, at eye level, and asks how to help
Uses lifts and ramps; checks the route is clear
Places luggage within reach and shows accessible features
Explains the emergency procedure and informs the front desk

practical1.title: Role play: room a guest from the front desk to the room
practical1.brief: Use the Centre's training room or a mock guest room set up with a bed, a luggage rack, a phone, an air conditioning remote and a safe or a box marked "safe". Each member in turn rooms one "guest" (another member or the assessor) with two or three pieces of luggage: greet the guest, take the key folder from the "desk" without saying the room number aloud, count and check the bags, load the trolley, lead the guest to the room, knock and open the door, place the bags on the rack, explain the room features, handle one problem the assessor gives (for example, the safe will not open or the room is not cleaned), leave politely and fill in a rooming slip. Members who are not rooming play guests or the desk agent. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and every member's rooming slip to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A mock guest room with a bed, luggage rack, phone, air conditioning remote and safe (or a box marked "safe")
A desk with key card folders, made-up registration cards and a made-up arrivals list
A luggage trolley and 3 pieces of luggage per guest (suitcases, a garment bag, a small bag)
Rooming slips (or a bell log) and pens
A fire escape plan for the back of the door and a guest directory
photos: The key folder handed over, with the room number written, not spoken
Luggage counted and loaded correctly on the trolley
Leading the guest to the room
Knocking and opening the door, lights on, guest let in first
Bags placed on the luggage rack, not the bed
Explaining a room feature (safe, air conditioning or phone)
checklist: Greeted the guest by title and surname and gave their own name
Counted the bags with the guest, checked for damage and lifted safely
Loaded and moved the trolley safely (heavy bags at the bottom)
Knocked, opened the door, switched on the lights and let the guest enter first
Placed the bags on the rack and explained at least five room features correctly
Handled the problem politely and called the desk where needed
Asked if anything else was needed, left politely and completed the rooming slip correctly
safety: Lift with bent knees and a straight back, keep loads close and get help with heavy bags
Do not overload the trolley; push it, and keep it under control on ramps and in doorways
Keep corridors and doorways clear of bags and cables
Use only made-up guest names and details

practical2.title: Plan and carry out the arrival and rooming of a family at a villa
practical2.brief: A family of four (two adults and two children) is arriving at a villa this afternoon. As a group, first prepare the paperwork: a short arrivals sheet for the family (names, arrival time, special requests such as a baby cot and a nut allergy), a room plan showing which bedroom each guest will use, and a one-page "villa welcome checklist" of everything to show and explain (gate and alarm, locks, air conditioning, pool rules, safe, Wi-Fi, how to call staff, emergency numbers and the fire exit). Then act out the arrival: welcome at the door with a drink, introduce the "villa staff", carry the luggage to the bedrooms, give the house tour using your checklist, and confirm meal times and the allergy with the guests. Every member must play a staff role in at least one part of the arrival while others play the family. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the paperwork to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Paper, pens and markers, or a computer and printer
A mock villa area: a front door, a bedroom or two, and a pool or a sign marking the pool
Luggage for four guests and a luggage trolley if available
Welcome drinks (water or juice), glasses and a tray
A sample villa information folder and emergency numbers sheet
photos: The arrivals sheet and the room plan
The welcome at the door, with drinks on a tray
Luggage carried to the right bedrooms
A staff member explaining the pool rules or the gate and alarm
The checklist ticked off at the end of the tour
checklist: Helped prepare the arrivals sheet, room plan and welcome checklist
Greeted the family warmly by title and surname and introduced the staff
Handled and placed the luggage safely and in the right rooms
Explained security (gate, alarm, locks, safe) clearly
Explained the pool rules and child safety around the pool
Confirmed the nut allergy and passed it on to the cook
Explained how to call staff and the emergency numbers
Kept a friendly, professional manner and ticked off the checklist
safety: Lift luggage safely: bent knees, straight back, load close to the body
Keep children away from the pool edge during the role play; walk, do not run, near water
Carry the tray of drinks with the heavy items in the centre; wipe spills at once
Use only made-up names and details
